Triggers.value: A specific temperature on the skin
Beginning to feel detached or unreal

Memory.value: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.

Negative Appraisals.value: My reactions since the event show that I am a lousy coper
Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore
Nothing good can happen to me anymore

vignette: Rajiv is a 26-year-old South Asian man who has been working as an editor for three years. Married and deeply engaged with his work, Rajiv’s life was upended following a traumatic encounter with the police during which he witnessed the unjust arrest of an innocent individual. The event left him feeling helpless and profoundly affected by the injustice. Since that day, Rajiv has experienced intense reactions to specific triggers. A sudden drop in temperature or being alone with women often plunges him into a state of distress. He describes these moments as almost unbearably overwhelming, leaving him questioning his ability to cope with such feelings. “When I’m around my wife now,” he explains, “or when the air conditioning is too cold, everything feels like it’s about to fall apart.” These triggers not only disrupt his personal life but have also begun to affect his work environment, where he sometimes needs to leave a meeting if the room becomes uncomfortably cool or if there are women present. The memory of that traumatic event remains vivid and visceral. When Rajiv recalls what happened, he experiences an overwhelming sense of grief that feels almost suffocating. He often smells scents reminiscent of that day—like the stale air in the police station—and his body reenacts the physical sensations of the event as if it were happening again. “It’s like I’m right back there,” Rajiv says, visibly shaken by these involuntary recollections. These memories intensify Rajiv's negative appraisals about himself and his life. He feels like a lousy coper and questions whether anything in his life has any meaning anymore. The idea that nothing good can happen to him seems almost inescapable. “I keep thinking I’m never going to get better,” he admits, “and it’s hard to find hope or purpose.” His negative appraisals have a cyclical effect on both his memories and triggers. When Rajiv is convinced of his inability to cope effectively, the memory of the traumatic event becomes more vivid and painful. The grief and olfactory recall become almost unbearable, and he feels that his body is reliving the event once again. This deepens his sense of hopelessness and reinforces the belief that nothing good can happen to him. Similarly, Rajiv’s negative appraisals exacerbate his reactions to triggers. His self-doubt about coping makes each trigger more potent; the cold temperatures or women present in the room feel like insurmountable challenges rather than mere inconveniences. He feels detached and unreal when these triggers occur, as if he is not truly part of the world around him. Rajiv’s occupation has also been affected by his symptoms. His avoidance behaviors have made it difficult to focus on work tasks, particularly when collaborating with female colleagues or working in environments that remind him of the traumatic event. This has led to a noticeable decline in productivity and strained relationships at work. What finally brought Rajiv to seek help was the realization that his reactions were increasingly isolating him from both his family and his professional life. He is most afraid of losing control entirely, but he also hopes for a return to a sense of normalcy and purpose. “I just want to be able to handle these things,” he says with a mix of frustration and hope. Rajiv’s story illustrates the complex interplay between triggers, memories, and negative appraisals, creating a cycle that has progressively tightened around him since the traumatic event. Each component reinforces the others, making it difficult for Rajiv to find any relief from his distressing symptoms.
